title: An ALMA Disk Mass for the Candidate Protoplanetary Companion to FW Tau
question: Is the 1.3 mm continuum (disk) emission in FW Tau associated with the close binary FW Tau AB or the faint companion, and what is the dust mass?

what.value: 850 um flux 4.5 ± 1.1 mJy of FW Tau system

evidence.quote: noted a 4$\sigma$ detection of the system at 850 $\mu$m ($F_{\nu}=4.5 \pm 1.1$ mJy)

what.value: Companion position 2.28" separation, PA 296 deg, and 3.6 um magnitude

evidence.quote: from the FW Tau AB photocenter (cite: Kraus:2014lr)

recipe.method: CASA calibration, natural-weighted CLEAN with one phase-only self-cal iteration
Gaussian fit to emission, model of visibilities; unresolved

assumptions: Dust temperature ~10–20 K; opacity 2.3 cm^2/g at 1.3 mm

answer_key.quantity: 1.3 mm integrated flux of FW Tau C
Dust mass of FW Tau C
FW Tau AB flux upper limit
FW Tau AB dust mass limit

evidence.quote: corresponds to a dust mass limit of $\lesssim$0.1 $M_{\oplus}$
The 3$\sigma$ upper limit on the peak flux is $\sim$3 mJy beam$^{-1}$ in a single 20 km s$^{-1}$-wide channel.

not_stated_but_needed: Image size and cell size, CLEAN threshold/mask and iterations
Dust mass equation details, gas-to-dust ratio, distance used
Derivation of the 3 sigma AB upper limit of 90 uJy and 0.1 Earth mass
score_reason: Short observation and simple analysis, but imaging parameters and CASA version are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from a Cycle 1 project and the simple flux measurement is numeric, though public status is not stated by the paper.
